source_batch.unit_label: Module B unit 7: Liquidity Risk Management

facts.statement: Liquidity is a bank's capacity to fund increases in assets and meet expected and unexpected cash and collateral obligations at reasonable cost and without unacceptable losses; liquidity risk is the inability to meet obligations as they fall due without adversely affecting the bank's financial condition, and it mainly shows up as funding liquidity risk (the risk of not meeting expected and unexpected current and future cash flows and collateral needs without affecting daily operations or financial condition) and market liquidity risk (the risk that a position cannot easily be offset or eliminated at the prevailing market price because of inadequate market depth or disruption). Liquidity problems arise from mismatches in the timing of inflows and outflows; a maturing liability is an outflow and a maturing asset an inflow, and banks are maturity transformation agents because deposits are short and advances long. A bank is solvent if the realisable value of its assets exceeds its outside liabilities; a bank can be solvent and liquid, liquid but not solvent, solvent but not liquid, or neither, and should be both. Internal drivers include heavy off-balance sheet exposure, reliance on short-term wholesale deposits, negative maturity gaps, asset growth outpacing funds, concentration of deposits in short tenors and thin holdings of liquid government securities; external drivers include sensitive depositors, economic shocks, slow growth, falling trust in banks and sudden withdrawals. The courseware calls liquidity risk the ICU risk because it lies in the short term.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 481-483, sections 17.1 to 17.4; Directions paragraph 19

facts.statement: The Basel Committee's Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision (published September 2008 and reviewed in January 2019, set out in Annex IV of the Directions) are thirteen: Principle 1, a robust framework and a cushion of unencumbered high quality liquid assets, with supervisors assessing both framework and position; governance: Principle 2 (a liquidity risk tolerance suited to the strategy), 3 (senior management develops strategy and policies; the board reviews and approves them at least annually), 4 (liquidity costs, benefits and risks in internal pricing, performance measurement and new product approval); measurement and management: Principle 5 (identify, measure, monitor and control, with cash flow projections), 6 (monitor within and across legal entities, business lines and currencies), 7 (diversified funding strategy), 8 (intraday liquidity), 9 (collateral management), 10 (regular stress tests), 11 (a formal contingency funding plan), 12 (a cushion of unencumbered high quality liquid assets); and public disclosure: Principle 13.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 483-486, section 17.5; Directions Annex IV (pp. 157-161)

facts.statement: Governance under the Directions has four tiers. The Board has overall responsibility for liquidity risk, decides strategy, policies and procedures in line with the liquidity risk tolerance, ensures the tolerance is understood at all levels, understands the liquidity risk profile of all branches, subsidiaries and associates, sets executive lines of authority and formulates or reviews the contingency funding plan; it or its committee reviews policies at least annually, approves internal limits for stock ratios and approves, with the Risk Management Committee, internal prudential limits on cumulative mismatches across all time buckets. The Risk Management Committee, reporting to the Board and consisting of the CEO or CMD and heads of the credit, market and operational risk committees, evaluates liquidity risk and its interaction with other risks. The Asset Liability Management Committee (ALCO), headed by the CEO, CMD or an Executive Director, ensures adherence to the Board's tolerance and limits and implements the strategy; its functions include deciding the maturity profile and mix of incremental assets and liabilities, the source and mix of liabilities, the structure and controls for liquidity risk, operational independence of the function, adequacy of cash flow projections, review of stress scenarios and contingency plan, the transfer pricing policy, and reporting the liquidity profile to the Board or Risk Management Committee. The ALM Support Group, of operating staff, analyses, monitors and reports the liquidity profile to ALCO and prepares forecasts and simulations.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 486-487, section 17.6; Directions paragraphs 6 to 18 and 21 to 28

facts.statement: The liquidity risk management policy spells out the liquidity risk tolerance, funding strategies, prudential limits, the system for measuring, assessing and reporting liquidity, the stress testing framework, liquidity planning under alternative scenarios including the contingency funding plan, the nature and frequency of management reporting and periodic review of projection assumptions; it also covers individual currencies, legal entities and business lines and limits transfers of liquidity. The Board sets an explicit liquidity risk tolerance defining the level of risk the bank is willing to assume, reflecting its financial condition and funding capacity, so that it can withstand a prolonged period of institution-specific and market-wide stress; it may be expressed through tolerance levels for maturities under the flow approach (keeping cash flow mismatches in buckets up to 30 days at minimum levels), through limits on stock ratios, or through minimum survival horizons under severe but plausible stress scenarios. The strategy must suit the nature, scale and complexity of the activities and identify primary sources of funding for daily operating outflows. Identification covers each major on and off-balance sheet position, embedded options and other contingent exposures, in all currencies in which the bank is active.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 487-489, sections 17.7 and 17.8.1; Directions paragraphs 29 to 33 and 46 to 48

facts.statement: Two approaches measure liquidity. The flow approach tracks cash flow mismatches through the structural liquidity statement (SLS), placing cash flows in time buckets by residual maturity or projected behaviour; the net of inflows and outflows in each bucket is the starting point for the future surplus or deficit. The time buckets are next day (day 1), 2-7 days, 8-14 days, 15-30 days, 31 days to 2 months, over 2 to 3 months, over 3 to 6 months, over 6 months to 1 year, and longer buckets up to over 15 years in the annexure. The SLS has five parts: domestic currency (Indian operations), foreign currency (Indian operations), combined Indian operations, overseas branch operations and consolidated bank operations. The domestic statement is prepared daily and reported to the Reserve Bank fortnightly (A1, A2 and A3 fortnightly, overseas part B monthly, consolidated part C quarterly); the courseware describes the same parts. Banks analyse behavioural maturity (rollover of maturing items, items with no stated maturity, draw-downs, contingent items), validate the assumptions by variance analysis at least once in six months, and track prepayments, premature closure and options. While mismatches up to one year give early warning, the main focus is the short term up to 30 days; the net cumulative negative mismatch in the next day, 2-7 days, 8-14 days and 15-30 days buckets must not exceed 5, 10, 15 and 20 per cent of the cumulative cash outflows of the respective bucket, and banks also set internal limits for all buckets with Board or Risk Management Committee approval. The stock approach is a point-in-time ratio view that does not reveal the intrinsic liquidity profile or future behaviour; the flow approach is forward looking and so superior.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 489 and 493-494; Directions paragraphs 34 to 39, 42 and 43, 283

facts.statement: Banks may monitor seven illustrative stock ratios against internally defined Board approved limits at the solo level and for major currencies: (1) (volatile liabilities - temporary assets) / (earning assets - temporary assets); (2) core deposits / total assets; (3) (loans + mandatory SLR + mandatory CRR + fixed assets) / total assets; (4) (loans + mandatory SLR + mandatory CRR + fixed assets) / core deposits; (5) temporary assets / total assets; (6) temporary assets / volatile liabilities; (7) volatile liabilities / total assets. Volatile liabilities are deposits plus borrowings and bills payable up to one year (borrowings include from the Reserve Bank, call and other institutions, and refinance; current and savings deposits reported as payable within one year are included), letters of credit in full, credit-conversion-factor weighted other contingent credit and commitments, and swap funds (buy/sell) up to one year. Temporary assets are cash, excess CRR balances with the Reserve Bank, balances with banks, bills purchased or discounted up to one year, investments up to one year and swap funds (sell/buy) up to one year. Earning assets are total assets less fixed assets, balances in current accounts with other banks, other assets excluding leasing, and intangible assets. Core deposits are all deposits (including current and savings deposits) above one year as reported in the SLS plus net worth. The courseware gives industry averages of 40, 50, 80, 150, 40, 60 and 60 per cent for the seven ratios; the Directions do not give them.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 489-490, section 17.9; Directions paragraphs 40 and 41 and Table 1

facts.statement: Stress testing is an integral part of governance and is done regularly for short-term and protracted bank-specific and market-wide scenarios, singly and in combination, taking account of products, off-balance sheet items and funding sources; assumptions are conservative and documented. A bank may assume an institution-specific crisis lasting no less than five business days and a general market crisis or combined scenario lasting no less than one calendar month. Results are discussed by ALCO, used to identify and quantify sources of strain, to build the liquidity cushion and shape the contingency funding plan; results and actions are documented, vulnerabilities are reported to the Board, a plan of action is charted at once, and the Department of Supervision of the Reserve Bank is informed immediately. A contingency funding plan (CFP) responds to severe disruptions that affect the bank's ability to fund activities in a timely manner at reasonable cost; it covers bank-specific and market-wide stress, contains details of available contingency funding sources and amounts, escalation and prioritisation procedures and the lead time to tap each source, defines roles, authority to invoke it, a crisis team and alternates, deals with how to contact external parties such as supervisors and the central bank, may include contingency funding lines or reciprocal lines with other banks, is tested regularly and reviewed by the Board at least annually.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 490-491, sections 17.10 and 17.11; Directions paragraphs 67 to 73

facts.statement: A reliable management information system gives the Board and ALCO timely forward-looking information on the liquidity position in all currencies, by subsidiary or branch in each country and on an aggregate group basis, in normal and stress situations; it captures all sources of liquidity risk including contingent risks and new activities and can supply more granular and time sensitive information in stress. Liquidity reports include cash flow projections and gaps, asset and funding concentrations, critical assumptions, funding availability, compliance with regulatory and internal limits, results of stress tests, key early warning or risk indicators, status of contingent funding sources and collateral usage. Internal controls: a bank has systems and procedures to ensure adherence to its liquidity policies and the adequacy of the management function; management ensures that an independent party regularly reviews the liquidity risk management process, covering compliance with regulatory instructions and its own policy, and reports non-compliance for prompt corrective action consistent with the Board approved policy. Early warning signals may include negative publicity, rising potential for deterioration in asset quality, widening debt or credit default swap spreads, and concerns over off-balance sheet funding; a bank also needs effective communication with counterparties, rating agencies and stakeholders to limit reputation contagion.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 486, 492-494, sections 17.5, 17.15 and 17.17; Directions paragraphs 49 and 50

facts.statement: Overseas operations: the bank's liquidity policy provides detailed procedures for overseas branches and subsidiaries to manage operational liquidity, with short-term liquidity delegated to local treasury; an SLS for overseas operations is prepared country-wise daily and reported monthly to the Reserve Bank, and the 5, 10, 15 and 20 per cent tolerance limits on net cumulative negative mismatches apply to overseas operations country-wise as well. Broad norms: no voluntary risk exposures beyond ten years; broaden long-term resources consistent with long-term assets; long-term resources not below 70 per cent of long-term assets and long and medium-term resources together not below 80 per cent of long and medium-term assets; controls applied currency-wise to each currency that is 10 per cent or more of the consolidated overseas balance sheet, with no netting of inter-currency positions or maturity gaps; short-term means maturing within six months, medium-term six months and longer but within three years, and long-term three years and longer; monitoring is centralised in the bank's International Division, which reviews the structural maturity mismatch position quarterly and reports to top management. Foreign currency liquidity in domestic operations is measured through Part A2 of the liquidity return, with a separate strategy for each major currency based on stress test outcomes. The Directions apply to commercial banks other than small finance banks, payments banks and local area banks.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 491-494, sections 17.12 to 17.14 and 17.16; Directions paragraphs 3, 44, 45 and 74

payload.title: Liquidity, liquidity risk and what drives it
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Liquidity** = **capacity to fund asset growth and meet expected and unexpected cash and collateral obligations at reasonable cost without unacceptable loss**. **Liquidity risk** = **inability to meet obligations as they fall due** without hurting the bank's financial condition.

| Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Funding liquidity risk** | **cannot meet expected and unexpected cash flows and collateral needs** without harming operations |
| **Market liquidity risk** | **cannot easily offset a position at the prevailing price** because of **thin markets or disruption** |

- Cause: **timing mismatch** of inflows and outflows; banks do **maturity transformation** (**short deposits, long loans**).
- **Solvent** = **assets exceed outside liabilities**. A bank may be **solvent and liquid, liquid not solvent, solvent not liquid, or neither**; it must be **both**.
- **Internal drivers**: **off-balance sheet exposure, wholesale short-term funding, negative gaps, asset growth beyond funds, short-tenor deposit concentration, few liquid government securities**.
- **External drivers**: **sensitive depositors, economic shocks, slow growth, falling trust, sudden withdrawals**.

payload.title: The thirteen Basel principles for liquidity risk
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Group | Principles |
| --- | --- |
| **Fundamental** | **1**: **robust framework** and a **cushion of unencumbered high quality liquid assets**; supervisors check **framework and position** |
| **Governance** | **2** **liquidity risk tolerance**; **3** **senior management strategy**, **board approves at least annually**; **4** **liquidity costs in internal pricing, performance and new products** |
| **Measurement and management** | **5** **identify, measure, monitor, control** with **cash flow projections**; **6** **entities, business lines, currencies**; **7** **diversified funding**; **8** **intraday liquidity**; **9** **collateral**; **10** **stress tests**; **11** **contingency funding plan**; **12** **cushion of high quality liquid assets** |
| **Disclosure** | **13** **public disclosure** |

(Published **September 2008**, **reviewed January 2019**; set out in **Annex IV** of the Reserve Bank's Directions.)

payload.title: Four tiers of liquidity governance
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Tier | Role |
| --- | --- |
| **Board** | **overall responsibility**; sets **strategy, policy, tolerance**; **reviews policies at least yearly**; approves **stock ratio limits**; **formulates or reviews the contingency funding plan** |
| **Risk Management Committee** | **reports to the Board**; **CEO or CMD plus heads of credit, market and operational risk committees**; **evaluates liquidity risk and its interaction with other risks** |
| **ALCO** | **headed by the CEO, CMD or an Executive Director**; **ensures adherence to the Board's limits** and **implements strategy**; decides **maturity profile and mix of new assets and liabilities**, **funding sources**, **transfer pricing**, **stress scenarios**; **reports to the Board or RMC** |
| **ALM Support Group** | **operating staff**; **analyses, monitors and reports** to ALCO; prepares **forecasts and simulations** |

payload.title: Policy, tolerance and strategy
The flow approach and the structural liquidity statement
payload.core_explanation_md:
| | **Flow approach** | **Stock approach** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Looks at** | **future cash flow mismatches by time bucket** | **ratios at a point in time** |
| **Strength** | **forward looking; superior** | **simple; benchmark ratios** |
| **Weakness** | needs **behavioural assumptions** | **shows past; hides the intrinsic profile** |

**SLS time buckets** (residual maturity): **day 1, 2-7, 8-14, 15-30 days, 31 days to 2 months, 2-3 months, 3-6 months, 6 months-1 year**, then longer.

**Five parts**: **domestic currency; foreign currency; combined Indian operations; overseas branches; consolidated bank**. **Prepared daily; reported fortnightly (A1, A2, A3), monthly (overseas, B), quarterly (consolidated, C)**.

**Limits** on **net cumulative negative mismatch** as a share of **cumulative outflows**: **day 1: 5%; 2-7 days: 10%; 8-14 days: 15%; 15-30 days: 20%**.

**Behavioural analysis** (**rollover, no-maturity items, draw-downs**) with **variance analysis at least every six months**; **focus is up to 30 days**.

payload.title: The seven stock ratios
payload.core_explanation_md:
| # | Ratio | Reads as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1** | **(Volatile liabilities − Temporary assets) ÷ (Earning assets − Temporary assets)** | **volatile money funding earning assets** |
| **2** | **Core deposits ÷ Total assets** | **stable funding base** |
| **3** | **(Loans + SLR + CRR + Fixed assets) ÷ Total assets** | **illiquid share of the balance sheet** |
| **4** | **(Loans + SLR + CRR + Fixed assets) ÷ Core deposits** | **illiquid assets financed by core deposits** |
| **5** | **Temporary assets ÷ Total assets** | **liquid assets held** |
| **6** | **Temporary assets ÷ Volatile liabilities** | **cover of liquid assets over volatile funds** |
| **7** | **Volatile liabilities ÷ Total assets** | **volatile funding of the balance sheet** |

**Volatile liabilities**: **deposits and borrowings up to 1 year, letters of credit in full, weighted contingents, swap funds (buy/sell) up to 1 year**. **Temporary assets**: **cash, excess CRR, balances with banks, bills up to 1 year, investments up to 1 year, swap funds (sell/buy)**. **Core deposits** = **deposits above 1 year + net worth**.

**Limits are internal and Board approved**. The **courseware's industry averages** (40, 50, 80, 150, 40, 60, 60%) **are not in the Directions**.

payload.title: Stress testing and the contingency funding plan
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Stress tests**: **regular**, **short and protracted**, **bank-specific and market-wide**, **singly and combined**; **conservative, documented assumptions**.

| Scenario | Minimum period |
| --- | --- |
| **Institution-specific crisis** | **five business days** |
| **General market or combined crisis** | **one calendar month** |

**Use**: **ALCO discusses results**; **build the cushion and adjust the profile**; **shape the contingency plan**. **Vulnerability: report to the Board, plan at once, inform the Reserve Bank's Department of Supervision immediately**.

**Contingency funding plan** must show: **available sources and amounts**, **escalation and prioritisation steps**, **lead time to tap each source**, **who can invoke it** (crisis team and alternates), **how to contact supervisors and central bank**; may include **contingency lines or reciprocal lines with other banks**. **Tested regularly; Board reviews at least annually**.

payload.title: Management information and internal controls
payload.core_explanation_md:
**MIS** gives the **Board and ALCO timely, forward-looking** data **in all currencies**, **by entity and for the group**, in **normal and stress** conditions, covering **contingent risks and new activities**.

**Reports include**: **cash flow projections and gaps; concentrations; key assumptions; funding availability; limit compliance; stress results; early warning indicators; contingent funding and collateral status**.

**Early warning signals**: **negative publicity, rising asset deterioration, widening debt or CDS spreads, concern about off-balance sheet funding**; plan **communication with counterparties and rating agencies** to limit **reputation contagion**.

**Internal controls**: **procedures to ensure policies are followed**; an **independent party regularly reviews** the process, covering **regulatory and own-policy compliance**, and **reports breaches for prompt corrective action**.

payload.title: Overseas operations, currencies and reporting
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Overseas branches and subsidiaries**: **local treasury manages operational liquidity** under the bank's policy; **SLS country-wise daily, reported monthly**; the **5/10/15/20% mismatch limits also apply**.

| Norm | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Tenor** | **no voluntary exposures beyond ten years** |
| **Long-term resources** | **at least 70% of long-term assets** |
| **Long + medium-term resources** | **at least 80% of long + medium-term assets** |
| **Definitions** | **short: within 6 months; medium: 6 months to under 3 years; long: 3 years and longer** |
| **Scope** | **each currency that is 10% or more of the consolidated overseas balance sheet**; **no netting of currencies or gaps** |
| **Monitoring** | **International Division**, **quarterly review to top management** |

**Foreign currency (domestic operations)**: **Part A2 of the liquidity return** and a **separate strategy per major currency** using **stress results**.

The Directions apply to **commercial banks other than small finance, payments and local area banks**.

payload.title: Reading the stock ratios
payload.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: a bank has total assets of ₹1,000 crore, earning assets of ₹850 crore, temporary assets of ₹150 crore, volatile liabilities of ₹300 crore, core deposits of ₹500 crore, and loans plus mandatory SLR plus mandatory CRR plus fixed assets of ₹700 crore. Compute four of the stock ratios.

worked_steps.description: Ratio 1: volatile money funding earning assets.
Ratio 3: illiquid share of the balance sheet.
Ratio 4: illiquid assets financed by core deposits.

self_check.prompt_text: What does a temporary assets to volatile liabilities ratio of 50% tell the ALCO?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Liquid assets cover only half of the volatile funds, so the bank may need more liquid investments or fewer volatile liabilities.

payload.title: Testing the short-term mismatch limits
payload.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: a bank's structural liquidity statement shows a net cumulative negative mismatch of ₹12 crore against cumulative outflows of ₹200 crore for the next day, and ₹130 crore against cumulative outflows of ₹800 crore up to the 15-30 day bucket. Check each against the Reserve Bank's limits.

worked_steps.description: Next day mismatch as a share of outflows.
15-30 day mismatch as a share of outflows.

payload.final_answer_with_unit: The next day bucket breaches its 5% limit; the 15-30 day bucket is within its 20% limit

self_check.prompt_text: Why might a bank breach the next day limit but stay within the 15-30 day limit?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The limits are set as a rising share of cumulative outflows, so the very short bucket is tightest, and a small outflow base can make a modest absolute gap exceed 5%.

payload.title: Overseas maturity norms
payload.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: a bank's overseas operations in one major currency hold long-term assets of ₹600 crore and long-term resources of ₹400 crore, and long and medium-term assets of ₹1,500 crore against long and medium-term resources of ₹1,250 crore. Test both tolerance levels.

worked_steps.description: Long and medium-term resources to assets.

payload.final_answer_with_unit: The long-term test fails by ₹20 crore; the long and medium-term test passes with a margin of ₹50 crore

self_check.prompt_text: Why can resources not be netted across currencies for these tests?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The Directions require the controls to be applied currency-wise for each currency that is 10 per cent or more of the overseas balance sheet, with no netting of inter-currency positions or gaps.

payload.stem_md: Which type of liquidity risk is the risk that a bank cannot easily offset a position at the prevailing market price because of inadequate market depth?

options.explanation_md: Concerns cash flows and collateral needs.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Market liquidity risk is the risk that a bank cannot easily offset or eliminate a position at the prevailing market price because of inadequate market depth or disruption.

payload.stem_md: A bank has assets worth more than its outside liabilities but cannot meet depositors' demands in the short term. It is
payload.correct_explanation_md: A bank is solvent when its realisable assets exceed outside liabilities; being unable to meet short-term demands makes it illiquid.

payload.stem_md: Which of the following is an internal banking factor that may lead to liquidity risk?

options.text_md: Decreasing trust of depositors in the banking sector
Heavy reliance on short-term wholesale deposits

payload.correct_explanation_md: Reliance on short-term corporate or wholesale deposits is an internal factor; the others are external.

payload.stem_md: How many principles are set out in Annex IV of the Reserve Bank's Asset Liability Management Directions, 2025 for sound liquidity risk management?
payload.correct_explanation_md: The Basel principles reproduced run from Principle 1 to Principle 13.

payload.stem_md: Which Basel liquidity principle requires a bank to maintain a cushion of unencumbered, high quality liquid assets as insurance against a range of stress scenarios?
payload.correct_explanation_md: Principle 12 requires a cushion of unencumbered, high quality liquid assets with no legal, regulatory or operational impediment to using them.

payload.stem_md: Which Basel liquidity principle asks the bank to incorporate liquidity costs, benefits and risks into internal pricing, performance measurement and new product approval?
payload.correct_explanation_md: Principle 4 aligns the risk-taking incentives of business lines with the liquidity risk their activities create.

payload.stem_md: Who has overall responsibility for the management of liquidity risk?
payload.correct_explanation_md: The Board is responsible for the overall management of liquidity risk and decides strategy, policies and procedures.

payload.stem_md: Which body, headed by the CEO, CMD or an Executive Director, implements the liquidity risk strategy and ensures adherence to the Board's limits?
payload.correct_explanation_md: ALCO is responsible for adherence to the risk tolerance and limits and for implementing the strategy.

payload.stem_md: Who decides the transfer pricing policy of the bank and makes liquidity costs and benefits part of strategic planning?
payload.correct_explanation_md: Deciding the transfer pricing policy and making liquidity costs and benefits integral to strategic planning is an ALCO function.

payload.stem_md: A bank sets its liquidity risk tolerance as the period it can survive under severe but plausible stress scenarios. This is described as
payload.correct_explanation_md: Tolerance may be expressed as minimum survival horizons under severe but plausible stress scenarios.

payload.stem_md: Which approach forecasts liquidity at different future points of time through time buckets?
payload.correct_explanation_md: The flow approach tracks cash flow mismatches across time buckets and so looks forward.

payload.stem_md: What is the limit on the net cumulative negative mismatch in the 8-14 days bucket?

options.text_md: 15 per cent of cumulative cash outflows

payload.correct_explanation_md: The limits are 5, 10, 15 and 20 per cent of cumulative outflows for next day, 2-7, 8-14 and 15-30 days.

payload.stem_md: How often is the structural liquidity statement for combined Indian operations reported to the Reserve Bank?
payload.correct_explanation_md: Parts A1, A2 and A3 are reported fortnightly; Part B monthly and Part C quarterly.

payload.stem_md: How often must a bank validate its behavioural assumptions by variance analysis, as a minimum?

options.text_md: At least once in six months
Only when the Reserve Bank asks

payload.correct_explanation_md: A bank undertakes variance analysis at least once in six months.

payload.stem_md: Which of the following is a component of the core deposits used in the stock ratios?

options.text_md: All deposits payable within one year
Deposits above one year plus net worth

payload.correct_explanation_md: Core deposits are all deposits above one year (including current and savings) plus net worth.

payload.stem_md: What do the numerator and denominator of the ratio of temporary assets to volatile liabilities compare?

options.text_md: Liquid assets against short-term, interest sensitive funds

payload.correct_explanation_md: The ratio measures the cover of liquid investments relative to volatile liabilities.

payload.stem_md: Which of these is counted among volatile liabilities?

options.text_md: Letters of credit, at their full outstanding amount

payload.correct_explanation_md: Letters of credit in full outstanding are included among volatile liabilities.

payload.stem_md: For an institution-specific crisis scenario, what is the minimum stress period a bank may assume?
payload.correct_explanation_md: An institution-specific crisis is assumed to last no less than five business days.

payload.stem_md: How long must a general market crisis or combined stress scenario be assumed to last, at least?
payload.correct_explanation_md: A general market crisis and a combined scenario last no less than one calendar month.

payload.stem_md: If stress test results show a vulnerability, which body must be informed immediately in addition to the Board?

options.text_md: The Department of Supervision of the Reserve Bank

payload.correct_explanation_md: Vulnerabilities are reported to the Board and the Department of Supervision, RBI is informed immediately.

payload.stem_md: Which of the following is an early warning signal of potential liquidity stress?

options.text_md: A fall in the bank's deposit interest rates
Widening debt or credit default swap spreads

payload.correct_explanation_md: Early warning signs include negative publicity, widening debt or CDS spreads and concern about off-balance sheet funding.

payload.stem_md: What is the minimum proportion of long-term resources to long-term assets for overseas operations?
payload.correct_explanation_md: Long term resources shall not fall below 70 per cent of long-term assets.

payload.stem_md: For the overseas maturity norms, which tenor is classed as medium-term?

options.text_md: Six months and longer but within three years

payload.correct_explanation_md: Medium-term refers to six months and longer but within three years.

payload.stem_md: The overseas maturity controls apply currency-wise to each currency that constitutes at least what share of the bank's consolidated overseas balance sheet?
payload.correct_explanation_md: The controls apply to each currency that individually constitutes 10 per cent or more of the consolidated overseas balance sheet.

payload.stem_md: Which department of a bank centralises monitoring of the overseas asset-liability mismatch?
payload.correct_explanation_md: The International Division controls the overseas mismatch on a consolidated, currency-wise basis and reviews it quarterly.

payload.stem_md: A bank has volatile liabilities of ₹420 crore and total assets of ₹1,200 crore. What is the ratio of volatile liabilities to total assets, in per cent, to two decimals?

numeric_rule.rounding_instruction: Give the answer to 2 decimal places.

numeric_rule.rounding_instruction: Give the answer to 2 decimal places.

unresolved: The Directions copy read is the mirror of the 28 November 2025 text; later amendments were not searched for. Submission time lags for liquidity returns are now set by the Filing of Supervisory Returns Directions, 2024, which was not read, so the courseware's time limits (within a week, 15 days, a month) are not tested.
The courseware's industry averages for the seven stock ratios are not in the Directions and are not tested as limits.

The Basel principles are taught from Annex IV of the Directions; the Basel Committee text itself was not read. Intraday liquidity (Chapter IV), the Liquidity Coverage Ratio and Net Stable Funding Ratio (Chapters V and VI) and interest rate risk (Chapter VII) are covered in later units, not here.
The courseware refers to time buckets aligned from 1 February 2016 and to a guideline of earlier years; the Directions of 2025 are used instead.

items.title: Liquidity, liquidity risk and what drives it
items.core_explanation_md:
**Liquidity** = **capacity to fund asset growth and meet expected and unexpected cash and collateral obligations at reasonable cost without unacceptable loss**. **Liquidity risk** = **inability to meet obligations as they fall due** without hurting the bank's financial condition.

| Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Funding liquidity risk** | **cannot meet expected and unexpected cash flows and collateral needs** without harming operations |
| **Market liquidity risk** | **cannot easily offset a position at the prevailing price** because of **thin markets or disruption** |

- Cause: **timing mismatch** of inflows and outflows; banks do **maturity transformation** (**short deposits, long loans**).
- **Solvent** = **assets exceed outside liabilities**. A bank may be **solvent and liquid, liquid not solvent, solvent not liquid, or neither**; it must be **both**.
- **Internal drivers**: **off-balance sheet exposure, wholesale short-term funding, negative gaps, asset growth beyond funds, short-tenor deposit concentration, few liquid government securities**.
- **External drivers**: **sensitive depositors, economic shocks, slow growth, falling trust, sudden withdrawals**.

| **Disclosure** | **13** **public disclosure** |

items.title: Four tiers of liquidity governance
items.core_explanation_md:
| Tier | Role |
| --- | --- |
| **Board** | **overall responsibility**; sets **strategy, policy, tolerance**; **reviews policies at least yearly**; approves **stock ratio limits**; **formulates or reviews the contingency funding plan** |
| **Risk Management Committee** | **reports to the Board**; **CEO or CMD plus heads of credit, market and operational risk committees**; **evaluates liquidity risk and its interaction with other risks** |
| **ALCO** | **headed by the CEO, CMD or an Executive Director**; **ensures adherence to the Board's limits** and **implements strategy**; decides **maturity profile and mix of new assets and liabilities**, **funding sources**, **transfer pricing**, **stress scenarios**; **reports to the Board or RMC** |
| **ALM Support Group** | **operating staff**; **analyses, monitors and reports** to ALCO; prepares **forecasts and simulations** |

items.title: The flow approach and the structural liquidity statement
items.core_explanation_md:
| | **Flow approach** | **Stock approach** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Looks at** | **future cash flow mismatches by time bucket** | **ratios at a point in time** |
| **Strength** | **forward looking; superior** | **simple; benchmark ratios** |
| **Weakness** | needs **behavioural assumptions** | **shows past; hides the intrinsic profile** |

**SLS time buckets** (residual maturity): **day 1, 2-7, 8-14, 15-30 days, 31 days to 2 months, 2-3 months, 3-6 months, 6 months-1 year**, then longer.

**Five parts**: **domestic currency; foreign currency; combined Indian operations; overseas branches; consolidated bank**. **Prepared daily; reported fortnightly (A1, A2, A3), monthly (overseas, B), quarterly (consolidated, C)**.

**Limits** on **net cumulative negative mismatch** as a share of **cumulative outflows**: **day 1: 5%; 2-7 days: 10%; 8-14 days: 15%; 15-30 days: 20%**.

**Behavioural analysis** (**rollover, no-maturity items, draw-downs**) with **variance analysis at least every six months**; **focus is up to 30 days**.

items.title: The seven stock ratios
items.core_explanation_md:
| # | Ratio | Reads as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1** | **(Volatile liabilities − Temporary assets) ÷ (Earning assets − Temporary assets)** | **volatile money funding earning assets** |
| **2** | **Core deposits ÷ Total assets** | **stable funding base** |
| **3** | **(Loans + SLR + CRR + Fixed assets) ÷ Total assets** | **illiquid share of the balance sheet** |
| **4** | **(Loans + SLR + CRR + Fixed assets) ÷ Core deposits** | **illiquid assets financed by core deposits** |
| **5** | **Temporary assets ÷ Total assets** | **liquid assets held** |
| **6** | **Temporary assets ÷ Volatile liabilities** | **cover of liquid assets over volatile funds** |
| **7** | **Volatile liabilities ÷ Total assets** | **volatile funding of the balance sheet** |

**Volatile liabilities**: **deposits and borrowings up to 1 year, letters of credit in full, weighted contingents, swap funds (buy/sell) up to 1 year**. **Temporary assets**: **cash, excess CRR, balances with banks, bills up to 1 year, investments up to 1 year, swap funds (sell/buy)**. **Core deposits** = **deposits above 1 year + net worth**.

**Limits are internal and Board approved**. The **courseware's industry averages** (40, 50, 80, 150, 40, 60, 60%) **are not in the Directions**.

items.title: Stress testing and the contingency funding plan
items.core_explanation_md:
**Stress tests**: **regular**, **short and protracted**, **bank-specific and market-wide**, **singly and combined**; **conservative, documented assumptions**.

| Scenario | Minimum period |
| --- | --- |
| **Institution-specific crisis** | **five business days** |
| **General market or combined crisis** | **one calendar month** |

**Use**: **ALCO discusses results**; **build the cushion and adjust the profile**; **shape the contingency plan**. **Vulnerability: report to the Board, plan at once, inform the Reserve Bank's Department of Supervision immediately**.

**Contingency funding plan** must show: **available sources and amounts**, **escalation and prioritisation steps**, **lead time to tap each source**, **who can invoke it** (crisis team and alternates), **how to contact supervisors and central bank**; may include **contingency lines or reciprocal lines with other banks**. **Tested regularly; Board reviews at least annually**.

items.title: Management information and internal controls
items.core_explanation_md:
**MIS** gives the **Board and ALCO timely, forward-looking** data **in all currencies**, **by entity and for the group**, in **normal and stress** conditions, covering **contingent risks and new activities**.

**Reports include**: **cash flow projections and gaps; concentrations; key assumptions; funding availability; limit compliance; stress results; early warning indicators; contingent funding and collateral status**.

**Early warning signals**: **negative publicity, rising asset deterioration, widening debt or CDS spreads, concern about off-balance sheet funding**; plan **communication with counterparties and rating agencies** to limit **reputation contagion**.

**Internal controls**: **procedures to ensure policies are followed**; an **independent party regularly reviews** the process, covering **regulatory and own-policy compliance**, and **reports breaches for prompt corrective action**.

items.title: Overseas operations, currencies and reporting
items.core_explanation_md:
**Overseas branches and subsidiaries**: **local treasury manages operational liquidity** under the bank's policy; **SLS country-wise daily, reported monthly**; the **5/10/15/20% mismatch limits also apply**.

| Norm | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Tenor** | **no voluntary exposures beyond ten years** |
| **Long-term resources** | **at least 70% of long-term assets** |
| **Long + medium-term resources** | **at least 80% of long + medium-term assets** |
| **Definitions** | **short: within 6 months; medium: 6 months to under 3 years; long: 3 years and longer** |
| **Scope** | **each currency that is 10% or more of the consolidated overseas balance sheet**; **no netting of currencies or gaps** |
| **Monitoring** | **International Division**, **quarterly review to top management** |

**Foreign currency (domestic operations)**: **Part A2 of the liquidity return** and a **separate strategy per major currency** using **stress results**.

The Directions apply to **commercial banks other than small finance, payments and local area banks**.

items.title: Reading the stock ratios
items.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: a bank has total assets of ₹1,000 crore, earning assets of ₹850 crore, temporary assets of ₹150 crore, volatile liabilities of ₹300 crore, core deposits of ₹500 crore, and loans plus mandatory SLR plus mandatory CRR plus fixed assets of ₹700 crore. worked_steps.description: Ratio 1: volatile money funding earning assets.
Ratio 3: illiquid share of the balance sheet.
Ratio 4: illiquid assets financed by core deposits.

self_check.prompt_text: What does a temporary assets to volatile liabilities ratio of 50% tell the ALCO?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Liquid assets cover only half of the volatile funds, so the bank may need more liquid investments or fewer volatile liabilities.

items.title: Testing the short-term mismatch limits
items.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: a bank's structural liquidity statement shows a net cumulative negative mismatch of ₹12 crore against cumulative outflows of ₹200 crore for the next day, and ₹130 crore against cumulative outflows of ₹800 crore up to the 15-30 day bucket. Check each against the Reserve Bank's limits.

worked_steps.description: Next day mismatch as a share of outflows.
15-30 day mismatch as a share of outflows.

items.final_answer_with_unit: The next day bucket breaches its 5% limit; the 15-30 day bucket is within its 20% limit

self_check.prompt_text: Why might a bank breach the next day limit but stay within the 15-30 day limit?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The limits are set as a rising share of cumulative outflows, so the very short bucket is tightest, and a small outflow base can make a modest absolute gap exceed 5%.
